title: Vanishing shifted Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $g$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to $\\{−1,1\\}$, and let $S$ be a set of coordinates in $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$. Form a function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube by multiplying the first coordinate by $g$ evaluated on the remaining coordinates. Its Fourier coefficient at the set obtained by shifting every coordinate of $S$ up by one is zero.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite set of coordinates in $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$
